'''Shinbetsu''' (神別) refers to one of the classifications of {{ill|Ancient history|en|Ancient history|qid=Q41493|lt=Ancient history}} {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|qid=Q17|lt=Japan}}'s [[Uji (clan)|clans]].

The ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|Shinsen Shōjiroku|qid=Q1045362|lt=Shinsen Shōjiroku}}'' compiled during the {{ill|Heian period|ar|فترة هييآن|ast|Periodu Heian|az|Heyan dövrü|bcl|Panahon ni Heian|bg|Хеян|bn|হেইআন যুগ|br|Marevezh Heian|ca|Període Heian|cs|Období Heian|de|Heian-Zeit|el|Περίοδος Χεϊάν|eo|Epoko Heian|es|Período Heian|eu|Heian aroa|fa|دوره هی‌آن|fi|Heian-kausi|fr|Époque de Heian|gl|Período Heian|he|תקופת הייאן|hi|हेआन काल|hr|Heian (razdoblje)|hu|Heian-kor|hy|Հեիան ժամանակաշրջան|id|Zaman Heian|it|Periodo Heian|ja|平安時代|ka|ჰეიანის პერიოდი|ko|헤이안 시대|la|Aevum Heian|lt|Hejano laikotarpis|mn|Хэйан|mr|हियन कालावधी|ms|Zaman Heian|my|ဟဲအိအန်ခေတ်|nl|Heianperiode|nn|Heian|no|Heian-perioden|oc|Epòca d'Heian|pl|Heian|ps|هېيان دوره|pt|Período Heian|ro|Perioada Heian|ru|Период Хэйан|sh|Heianski period|simple|Heian period|sk|Obdobie Heian|sl|Obdobje Heian|sq|Periudha Heian|sr|Хеиан период|sv|Heian|ta|ஹையன் காலகட்டம்|th|ยุคเฮอัง|tl|Panahong Heian|tr|Heian Dönemi|uk|Період Хейан|vi|Thời kỳ Heian|war|Panahon Heian|wuu|平安时代|zh|平安时代|zh_classical|平安朝|zh_min_nan|Heian sî-tāi|zh_yue|平安時代|qid=Q193292|lt=Heian period}} describes Shinbetsu alongside ''{{ill|Kōbetsu|ja|皇別}}'' and ''{{ill|Shoban|ja|諸蕃}}'', identifying the descendants of ''{{ill|Amatsukami|ja|天津神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/matsukami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天津神・国津神|comment=confirming this goes to Kunitsukami|qid=Q60994492|2=zh|3=天神 (日本神話)|4=fr|5=Amatsukami|6=mni|7=ꯑꯃꯠꯁꯨꯀꯃꯤ|comment=confirming this goes to Kunitsukami|qid=Q60994492|2=zh|3=天神 (日本神話)|4=fr|5=Amatsukami|6=mni|7=ꯑꯃꯠꯁꯨꯀꯃꯤ}}'' and ''{{ill|Kunitsukami|fr|Kunitsukami|it|Kunitsukami|ja|国津神|mni|ꯀꯨꯅꯤꯠꯁꯨꯀꯃꯤ|simple|Kunitsukami|zh|國津神|qid=Q60995523}}'' as "Shinbetsu" ("天神地祇之冑、謂之神別"). Furthermore, Shinbetsu is categorized into ''{{ill|Posterity of Heaven|ja|天孫|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q108278353}}'', ''{{ill|Amatsukami|ja|天津神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/matsukami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天津神・国津神|comment=confirming this goes to Kunitsukami|qid=Q60994492|2=zh|3=天神 (日本神話)|4=fr|5=Amatsukami|6=mni|7=ꯑꯃꯠꯁꯨꯀꯃꯤ|comment=confirming this goes to Kunitsukami|qid=Q60994492|2=zh|3=天神 (日本神話)|4=fr|5=Amatsukami|6=mni|7=ꯑꯃꯠꯁꯨꯀꯃꯤ}}'', and ''{{ill|Kunitsukami|fr|Kunitsukami|it|Kunitsukami|ja|国津神|mni|ꯀꯨꯅꯤꯠꯁꯨꯀꯃꯤ|simple|Kunitsukami|zh|國津神|qid=Q60995523}}'', with Tenson accounting for 109, Amatsukami for 265, and Kunitsukami for 30 entries. These classifications are thought to have ancient origins, as inferred from the concentration of ''{{ill|Omi (title)|en|Omi (title)|qid=Q2574718|lt=Omi}}'' titles among ''{{ill|Kōbetsu|ja|皇別}}'' clans and ''{{ill|Muraji|en|Muraji|qid=Q2735611|lt=Muraji}}'' titles among Shinbetsu clans under the pre-[[Ritsuryō system]].

The ancestral deity of a shinbetsu clan is their [[Oyagami]] and will also be an [[Ujigami]] although some clans may have other Ujigami such as the '''{{ill|Fujiwara clan|en|Fujiwara clan|qid=Q641628|lt=Fujiwara clan}}''' whose three Oyagami are [[Ame-no-Koyane]], [[Himegami]] and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshikumone|ja|天押雲根命}}, however the two are worshipped alongside two non-ancestral Ujigami: [[Takemikazuchi]]-o, and [[Futsunushi]]. The five are merged together into the composite deity {{ill|Kasuga-no-Kami|ja|春日神|fr|Kasuga_no_Kami}} worshipped at [[Kasuga-taisha]] and many other Kasuga shrines nationwide.
